### Rationale

Codex found real hardening gaps but no verdict-changing defect. The decision rule for this artifact: the plan BANS false FAILs (acceptance A4, §8 zero-FAIL sweep, K1) — neither reviewer demonstrated one on any realistic body; every verified Codex finding is either lenient-direction (false-PASS/evasion residual on a net-new detection layer, each with a visible skip/note), a pathological-input robustness gap whose failure mode is loud (crash or slow), or a design the approved plan itself prescribes verbatim (§4.5(b) working-copy read; §4.6 WARN lattice; §5.1 `stems[:40]`). Codex's Critical-severity magnitude claims do not survive contact with the code: the "10–30 second timeouts" per subprocess are timeout ceilings — a failing object probe measured ~15 ms — and the classification probe is short-circuited by `is_file()`, so "wedging the fleet-wide promotion gate" is unsupported. Against this, the Claude PASS rests on EXECUTED evidence Codex could not produce under its execution ban: 26 `-k verbatim` tests + 1102-test full file green, bare + full-ruleset ruff + policy pin clean, and an independent reviewer-run 2,569-body corpus sweep reproducing the implementer's 0 FAIL / 2 WARN exactly. Executed evidence outweighs speculative magnitude. Claude was right on the verdict; Codex's real findings are preserved as 4 persisted CONCERNs so the follow-through is ledger-gated rather than prose-only.
